'''''Crassothonna capensis''''' (previously '''''Othonna capensis'''''), also known as '''little pickles''' (USA)''', ruby necklace''' (Australia), '''Cape aster, Cape Othonna''', and '''Bobbejaankool''' (Afrikaans),<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Solomon|first=Lorraine|title=Othonna capensis|url=https://kumbulanursery.co.za/plants/othonna-capensis|access-date=28 April 2021|website=Kumbula Nursery}}</ref> is a [[species]] of the genus ''[[Crassothonna]]'' previously (''[[Othonna]]'') in the family [[Asteraceae]], and is a native of  the [[Eastern Cape]] of [[South Africa]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=van Jaarsveld|first=Ernst|date=2006|title=Othonna triplinervia|url=https://bioone.org/journals/cactus-and-succulent-journal/volume-78/issue-6/0007-9367(2006)78[316:OTANCD]2.0.CO;2/Othonna-triplinervia/10.2985/0007-9367(2006)78[316:OTANCD]2.0.CO;2.full|journal=Cactus and Succulent Journal|volume=78|issue=6 |pages=316–317|doi=10.2985/0007-9367(2006)78[316:OTANCD]2.0.CO;2 |s2cid=198149644 |via=BioOne|url-access=subscription}}</ref> It is a native [[highveld]] species that originates from the southern [[Drakensberg]] region.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=van Jaarsveld|first=Ernst|date=1998|title=The Highveld Garden|url=https://journals.co.za/doi/abs/10.10520/AJA00423203_1605|journal=Veld & Flora|volume=84|pages=17–21|via=Sabinet}}</ref>

== Description ==
This species is a low-growing, succulent, spreading ground cover with finger-like, blue-grey leaves, spirally arranged, which become tipped with maroon in dry conditions.<ref name=":0" /> It has yellow daisy-like flowers on long, slender stems.<ref name=":0" />

== Taxonomy ==
It was described by [[Liberty Hyde Bailey|L.H. Bailey]] in 1901 and published in the Cyclopedia of American Horticulture<ref>{{Cite book|last=Bailey|first=Liberty Hyde|title=Cyclopedia of American Horticulture|publisher=The Macmillan Company|year=1901|location=New York|pages=1180}}</ref> replacing the original description and name from 1865 ''Othonna crassifolia'' Harv. In turn, the genus was changed from ''Othonna'' by Nordenstam et al., who erected the new genus ''Crassothonna'' for the clade of ''Othonna'' species ''O. sedifolia, O. alba'' and ''O. capensis''.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Nordenstam|first1=B.|title=Systematics, Evolution and Biogeography of Compositae|last2=Pelser|first2=P. B.|last3=Kadereit|first3=J.W.|last4=Watson|first4=L.E.|publisher=International Association for Plant Taxonomy, Institute of Botany, University of Vienna|year=2009|isbn=9783950175431|location=Vienna, Austria|pages=503–521|chapter=Senecioneae}}</ref> The new name for this species is therefore ''Crassothonna capensis'' (L.H.Bailey) B.Nord. 

== Distribution and habitat ==
This species is endemic to the [[Eastern Cape|Eastern Cape Province]] in semi-arid [[Karoo]] scrub and dry, rocky flats, often in the partial protection of surrounding vegetation or rocks.<ref name=":0" /> 

== Cultivation ==
In cultivation, the species is commonly called little pickles in the USA or ruby necklace in Australia and is used for rockeries, terrariums, indoor hanging pots and outside [[xeriscaping]].
